Definition: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237; sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure:--gladly.
BiblicalUsage: Hedeos means gladly, with pleasure, and it shows up in three very different moods. In 2 Corinthians 11:19 Paul says the Corinthians gladly suffer fools, in Mark 6:20 Herod hears John gladly and does many things, and in Mark 12:37 the common people hear Jesus gladly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word asks me what I enjoy hearing: Herod liked John's preaching and still killed him, and the crowd liked Jesus and still left him; glad hearing is not the same as obeying.
